Convergence in r-th mean can be thought of as convergence of integrals (where
of course, in probability theory, integrals are equivalent to expectations).
Convergence in r-th mean is equivalent to [[convergence-in-norm]] on
[[lp-spaces|$L^p$ Spaces]]

**Definition (Convergence in r-th Mean)**
A sequence of random variables $\{X_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ on probability space
$(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P})$ is said to **converge in r-th mean** to $X$
for $r\geq 1$, denoted $X_n\stackrel{L^r}{\rightarrow}X$ $(n\rightarrow\infty)$
if
$$
\lim_{ n \to \infty } \mathbb{E}|X_{n}-X|^r = 0,
$$
and $\mathbb{E}|X_{n}|^r<\infty$ for all $n$.
